title: Extortion group n0n claims approximately 166 million database records from USA TODAY Co.; company has not confirmed, The420 reports
date_note: The420 says n0n posted the claim on 25 November; its page shows only an 'updated' day of 26 November.
summary: The420 reports that the extortion group n0n posted a claim on its leak site on 25 November to hold a subscriber identity database of approximately 166 million records from USA TODAY Co. (formerly Gannett). The figures come from the attackers and are not independently authenticated. The article says the company has not publicly confirmed an intrusion.
plain: A hacking group claims it stole approximately 166 million records from USA TODAY Co. The claim is unverified and the company has not confirmed it.
exec: An unverified claim of approximately 166 million records from USA TODAY Co.; the company has not publicly confirmed an intrusion, per The420.
geo_basis: country: the source gives no city for the victim

sources.name: The420.in: Hackers Claim 166 Million USA Today Records Stolen In New Cyberattack

validation.note: Only The420 read; Cybernews returned 403 and BreachSense is a tracker, so neither is cited.

evidence.quote: includes a large subscriber identity database containing approximately 166 million records
166 million database records would not necessarily represent 166 million different people

review.note: figure qualifier: source says approximately 166 million; added to title, summary, plain, exec and evidence
